title: Reconnect+ Support Worker
company: Supporting Futures Consulting Ltd - Agency - Contract
description:
Role: Reconnect+ Support Worker

Based: Lewisham/New Cross

Rate: £15.50 PAYE or £20ph umb

Start Date: ASAP

Duration: Temp ongoing

Hours: Mon Fri 9am 5pm

Our client, a specialist charity, are recruiting for a Reconnect+ Support Worker to provide specialist person centred support services to women with multiple needs such as substance misuse issues and/or mental health issues on release from prison.

Synopsis of duties:
- Take responsibility for the effective day to day management and smooth operation of the project.
- Complete star needs assessments; draft, implement and regularly review a trauma informed, person centred, support and action plan to meet the individual needs of women referred to the project.
- Carry out thorough risk assessments in conjunction with the women and any other relevant agencies, implement person centred risk management plan and regular reviews.
- Carry out initial assessments of new referrals.
- Provide effective advice and advocacy services to ensure that women receive their statutory rights in respect of housing, benefits, etc.
- Ensure effective partnership working with other relevant agencies.
- Provide resettlement advice and support to women who have left the project.
- Develop and run group sessions/activities which meet the needs of the women and aims of the project.
- Participate in the Out of Hours on call rota as required.
- Ensure that women accessing the Project understand and comply with the Service User Agreement and the terms of their occupancy agreements. Housing management
- Monitor Rent accounts weekly, ensuring that rent and service charge collection is maximised, and arrears minimised.
- Issue occupancy agreements and induct new service users into the service.
- Preparing rooms for residents as required
- Ensure that voids are actively managed and that empty rooms are let within the target timescales.
- Take appropriate action in respect of breaches of licence agreements in line with policy and in consultation with the manager.
- Carry out regular health and safety checks in line with policy.
- Ensure repairs are reported promptly and work completed within appropriate timescales, ensuring the continued provision of good quality housing, equipment, fixtures, furnishings, and fittings.
- Organise and facilitate night staff team meetings.
- Co-ordinate and oversee the night/weekend staffing rota.
- Ensure service user files and support plans and other written documents are accurately completed and clear, and that data is entered onto relevant computer/paper-based systems in a timely fashion.
- Provide accurate and timely information or data reports to the Deputy manager as requested.

Essential Requirements
- Experience of working/delivering support to women involved in the Criminal Justice System (CJS)
- Experienced in meeting the support needs of women and appropriately advocating on behalf of service users.
- Experience of working collaboratively with external agencies.
- Experience in creating and facilitating activities with a service user led approach
- Enhanced Adult and Child DBS on the update service or dated within the last 12 months

Supporting Futures Consulting acts as both an employer and an agency

title: Learning Support Worker
description:
- Learning Support Worker
- 1 to 1 support
- Post-16 college setting
- Temp to Perm contract
- £14 32 per hour
- September 2026

A specialist college with a provision for students with MLD, SLD, Autism and behavioural needs are looking for Learning Support Assistant to join their team to support a student on a 1 to 1 basis.

The Role

In this Learning Support Worker role, you will be supporting a student who has learning disabilities and behaviour difficulties on a 1 to 1 basis. The student requires personalised support to access learning and development sessions throughout the college day.

Your role will include:
- Providing tailored, one-on-one support using Makaton, assistive technology and learning resources.
- Collaborating with teaching staff to adapt and deliver activities
- Assisting the student with study skills, time management, and organisation
- Promoting independence, confidence, and social skills both inside and outside the classroom.
- Monitoring and recording progress, providing feedback to teaching staff, support teams and parents

The successful candidate will undertake five days training provided by the Local Authority prior to starting the position.

Person Specification:
- Experience in SEND / Support work
- Experience in behaviour support
- Lively and energetic approach
- Committed attitude

This role is offered on a full-time (5 days a week) basis and whilst initially offered on a contract basis will become a permanent position for the right candidate.

The Centre

This specialist centre is based in Camden is part of a larger post-16 London college. The centre currently provides education and care support to around 50 young people aged 16 to 25 with profound and multiple or severe learning difficulties, complex autism and/or physical difficulties. There is a dedicated and experienced management and staff team in place at the centre and they have excellent training and development programmes. The centre operates during term-time only and is easily accessible via public transport.

The Centre are open to applications from both experienced learning support assistants/support workers and those with a positive and caring attitude looking to pursue a career supporting young people in Special Educational Needs.

If this position is of interest, please apply with an up-to-date CV.

We have a policy to respond to all applications within three working days. However, because of the volume of applications, we are sometimes unable to reply to individual enquiries. If we have not contacted you within this specified time your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion. Philosophy Education is a Recruitment Business and is advertising this vacancy on behalf of one of its clients.

title: Personal Assistant (HR)
description:
Temporary Personal Assistant - Human Resources

Location: London, with occasional travel to a construction site in Suffolk
Contract: 3 months, with possible extension
Engagement: Inside IR35
Working Pattern: Hybrid - minimum 3 days per week in the office

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Temporary Personal Assistant to provide trusted, confidential and highly organised support to members of the Human Resources Leadership Team.

This is a fast-paced and demanding role, requiring an accomplished PA or senior administrator who can manage complex diaries, coordinate meetings and travel, prepare high-quality documentation and confidently communicate with senior stakeholders.

The role is required for an initial 3-month period while recruitment for the permanent position is ongoing, with the possibility of an extension.

Given the nature of the role, confidentiality, discretion and integrity are essential. You will regularly handle sensitive HR information and interact with senior leaders, government representatives, Members of Parliament, trade union officials and other external stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
Provide professional, accurate and reliable PA and administrative support to the HR Leadership Team.
Manage complex diaries, appointments and competing priorities across multiple projects.
Coordinate frequent and sometimes complex travel arrangements across the UK and France, including accommodation, transport and detailed itineraries.
Organise and coordinate internal and external meetings, including room bookings, meeting packs, agendas and associated documentation.
Attend HR meetings where required and provide administrative and coordination support.
Prepare correspondence, reports, presentations, letters and other professional documentation.
Maintain accurate contact lists, records, training and induction logs.
Ensure effective document management and classification in accordance with company procedures.
Act as a key point of contact for internal and external enquiries, screening calls and correspondence appropriately.
Communicate messages and decisions on behalf of the HR Leadership Team, resolving queries where appropriate and escalating when required.
Support the planning and delivery of internal and external HR events, dinners, conferences and stakeholder engagements.
Liaise with Finance regarding invoices, purchasing and local cost records.
Arrange the ordering and payment of goods and services through the relevant systems.
Support office administration and general services as required.
Maintain strict confidentiality when dealing with sensitive HR and business information.
Keep in contact with HR leaders when they are out of the office and ensure actions and issues are appropriately followed up.
Provide additional PA support across the wider project during periods of peak workload or short-term absence.
Work closely with the Executive Assistant to the Chief People Officer and other PAs to ensure effective team coverage.
About You

We are looking for a confident and capable PA who can operate with a high degree of trust and discretion and who is comfortable supporting senior stakeholders in a complex project environment.

You will be:

Highly organised, methodical and able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Proactive and able to work independently with minimal supervision.
Calm and professional when working under pressure and to tight deadlines.
An excellent communicator, comfortable dealing with people at all levels.
Discreet and trustworthy when handling confidential and sensitive information.
Flexible and adaptable, with the ability to respond to changing priorities.
A strong team player who is willing to provide support to colleagues when required.
Confident dealing with difficult or sensitive enquiries.
Highly attentive to detail and committed to producing professional, accurate work.
Essential Experience
Previous experience in a PA, Executive Assistant, Team Assistant or senior administrative support role.
Strong general administrative and secretarial experience.
Experience managing complex diaries and coordinating meetings.
Experience arranging travel, accommodation and itineraries.
Excellent working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Strong experience using Outlook or a similar diary and email management system.
Ability to adapt quickly to new systems and processes, with the confidence to help develop new administrative systems where required.
Proven ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.
Desirable Experience
Experience supporting senior leaders within a large or complex organisation.
Experience working with UK Government officials, MPs, trade unions or external agencies.
Experience within a major infrastructure, construction, energy or regulated environment.
An understanding of project management processes.
Experience or interest in communications and stakeholder engagement.
The Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Temporary PA to join a high-profile HR function supporting the delivery of a major UK infrastructure project.

You will work closely with senior HR leaders and play an important role in ensuring the smooth and effective operation of the HR function during a period of significant activity.

If you are a highly organised, discreet and proactive PA who enjoys working in a demanding environment and is confident supporting senior stakeholders, we would be keen to hear from you.

Please note: This role is Inside IR35, initially for 3 months, with potential for extension. The successful candidate will be required to work from the London office at least 3 days per week, with occasional travel to a construction site in Suffolk.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker at Plus Services

Are you a positive, engaging and caring person that wants to make a real difference to the world?

Do you think the greatest gift you can give is to make other people's lives better?

Do you believe that people living with Learning Disabilities and Autism should have happy fulfilling lives, with access to the Community and enjoy the same things the rest of us take for granted?

If you answered "Yes" to these 3 Questions then Plus has an amazing role for you !

Who are Plus Services?

Plus is one of the most respected Learning Disability and Autism Charities in London with a proud history stretching back more than 30 years. We have an amazing team that is dedicated to supporting people to live their best possible lives and we have literally changed people's worlds with the support we have provided.

Our Client Group is quite varied and during the recruitment process you would be specifically recruited to work with those that your personality, skills and experience would fit best with. Some have really challenging behaviour, but unless you had the capability to best serve those people you would be assigned to a different group. So, there is no need to worry about being out of your depth.

We also provide industry leading training and on-going support, so rest assured you will be ready for anything the job throws at you. I cannot promise you it will be easy, but I can promise you it will be worth it. And when you go home you will know you have made a massive difference and the world is a slightly better place as a result of your efforts.

Who are you?

You are a caring, compassionate and capable individual? You could be either already working within Social Care or are thinking about joining the sector. We recognise everyone, regardless of their personal history, talents, abilities and unique personal qualities

What does matter is you must care and you must want to enhance the lives of the people who we support and rely on us.

You will need to be comfortable spending large amounts of your day one-to-one with the Service Users, there is no leaping from client to client here with 15 minute blocks. You will need to be happy supporting people to learn new skills and become independent. And you will need to thrive on taking people out into the big wide world, expanding their horizons, bringing a smile to their faces and adding a spring in to their step.

To be considered for the role you will need to be able to:
- Do your share of weekend shifts, sleep-ins, waking nights and bank holidays.
- Be physically fit and able to move freely and physically and to support service users who may be physically dependent.
- Have a supportive attitude and want to help individuals to maximise their lives.
- You must be able to support people with Learning Disabilities who have different ways of expressing themselves
- Be eligible to work in the UK

In return we offer opportunities for professional development and real job satisfaction. We can help you to develop your professional skills and knowledge and progress toward recognised qualifications such as Diploma in Adult & Social Care levels 3/4/5.

We are reviewing applications on a regular basis as part of our ongoing recruitment process and we are committed to ensuring all candidates are treated fairly

title: Children's Support Worker
description:
Location: Bexley
Role: School Support Worker / SEND Learning Support Assistant
Contract: Full-Time, Long-Term

About the Role

We are currently recruiting School Support Workers to join a welcoming and supportive specialist SEND school in Bexley.

The school supports secondary-aged pupils with severe learning difficulties, profound and multiple learning difficulties, complex needs and physical disabilities. Many pupils require a high level of individualised support throughout the school day, so we are looking for patient, caring and reliable individuals who are confident providing both learning and personal care support.

This is a hands-on role and would particularly suit candidates with previous experience within SEND schools, healthcare, residential care, support work or complex-needs settings.

Key Responsibilities
- Providing 1:1 and small-group support to pupils with complex SEND.
- Supporting pupils with SLD, PMLD, physical disabilities and additional needs.
- Assisting pupils to access learning and participate in classroom activities.
- Supporting pupils with their communication, independence and social development.
- Providing personal care, including toileting and changing where required.
- Supporting pupils with mobility, moving and positioning in line with individual care plans and training.
- Supporting pupils during break times, lunchtimes and activities throughout the school day.
- Following individual education, behaviour, medical and care plans.
- Working closely with teachers, therapists and other support staff.
- Promoting pupils' safety, dignity, independence and wellbeing at all times.
- Following the school's safeguarding procedures and maintaining professional boundaries.

The Ideal Candidate

We would love to hear from candidates who:
- Have experience supporting children, young people or adults with additional or complex needs.
- Have experience within SEND, healthcare, care, residential or support-work environments.
- Are comfortable providing personal and intimate care where required.
- Are patient, compassionate and able to remain calm in challenging situations.
- Are comfortable working with pupils who may have limited or non-verbal communication.
- Are physically able and willing to support pupils with mobility needs following appropriate training.
- Can build positive and trusting relationships with vulnerable young people.
- Are reliable, proactive and able to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.

Experience with PMLD, SLD, Autism, complex medical needs, hoisting, manual handling, personal care or alternative communication methods would be highly desirable.

Apply today to find out more about this School Support Worker opportunity in Bexley.

We are looking for a Support Worker who will provide high-quality, person-centred care and support to an individual living with a spinal cord injury (C4 ASIA C tetraplegia). The role focuses on promoting independence, supporting physical and emotional wellbeing, assisting with daily living activities, and maintaining a safe and supportive environment.

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
description:
Behaviour Support Assistant

Location: Sheffield, S9
Job Type: Full-time
Start Date: ASAP

We are looking for an experienced, resilient and compassionate Behaviour Support Assistant to join a specialist educational setting in Sheffield, S9, supporting students with complex additional needs.

This is a rewarding but challenging role, and previous experience working directly with students with severe Autism and ADHD is essential. We are looking for someone who understands that behaviour is a form of communication and who has the confidence, patience and consistency required to support young people with complex behavioural and sensory needs.

The Role

As a Behaviour Support Assistant, you will work closely with teaching and pastoral staff to provide high-quality, individualised support to students. You will help create a safe, structured and positive learning environment where students can develop academically, socially and emotionally.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing 1:1 and small-group support to students with severe Autism and ADHD.
- Supporting students who may present with complex or challenging behaviours.
- Implementing individual behaviour support plans and agreed strategies consistently.
- Helping students to regulate their emotions and manage anxiety, frustration and sensory overload.
- Using appropriate de-escalation and positive behaviour-support techniques.
- Building trusting and meaningful relationships with students.
- Supporting students to engage with learning and develop independence.
- Working closely with teachers, SEN staff, families and external professionals.
- Maintaining a calm, predictable and structured environment.
- Recording and communicating relevant information regarding behaviour, progress and safeguarding.

Essential Experience

Candidates must have previous hands-on experience working with students or young people with severe Autism and ADHD.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience supporting young people who may:
- Display challenging, distressed or high-risk behaviours.
- Experience sensory overload or emotional dysregulation.
- Have difficulty with communication and social interaction.
- Require highly structured routines and individualised support.
- Need consistent behaviour-management and de-escalation strategies.
- Present with behaviours that can include aggression, self-injury, absconding or significant emotional distress.

Experience within specialist schools, SEN provisions, residential settings, behavioural services or similar environments would be highly desirable.

The Ideal Candidate

You will be:
- Experienced in supporting young people with severe Autism and ADHD.
- Calm, patient and emotionally resilient.
- Confident managing challenging situations without becoming reactive.
- Consistent in following behaviour-support strategies and boundaries.
- Able to build positive relationships with students who may initially struggle to trust adults.
- Observant and able to recognise triggers, patterns and changes in behaviour.
- A strong communicator and team player.
- Committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.
- Passionate about helping students achieve their potential, regardless of the challenges they face.

Please note: this is not a role where general classroom experience alone will be sufficient. Due to the complexity of the students' needs, demonstrable experience supporting young people with severe Autism and ADHD is an essential requirement.

Why Join Us?

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Behaviour Support Assistant to make a genuine difference in the lives of young people with complex needs. You will be part of a supportive team and will receive ongoing guidance and development to help you succeed in the role.

If you have the specialist experience, resilience and commitment required to support students with severe Autism and ADHD, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today to be considered for this rewarding opportunity in Sheffield, S9.
